harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created `opsbot` on both Ubuntu 7.10 nodes, configured locked-password/key-only SSH, and enabled node1→node2 command execution as `opsbot`. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities. The installed OS release and 2.6.22 kernel were preserved.
actions_performed: Created locked `opsbot` accounts on node1 and node2
Generated a legacy-compatible 2048-bit RSA key as `opsbot` on node1
Installed authorized keys with correct ownership and permissions
Added and validated explicit per-user key-only sshd policy
Verified node1→node2 remote command execution as `opsbot`
Verified password-only authentication is rejected on both nodes
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified persistent recovery

evidence.requirement: opsbot accounts and SSH key configuration
evidence.summary: Shows locked accounts, generated RSA key, installed authorized key, and secure file permissions.

evidence.requirement: Key-based node1-to-node2 command access and password rejection
evidence.summary: Commands executed remotely with uid opsbot; password-only authentication was rejected before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Legacy OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained unchanged on both nodes.
Captures healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered sshd, account, keys, policy, and SSH access.
Captures healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered sshd/account/key state, and successful node1→node2 access.
